findings.reason: A concrete frequency-plane picture materially clarifies the distinct roles of a measured normal arc, its full signed frequency lines, and analytic continuation to unmeasured frequencies. The authentic original tiles contain no such illustration. The general open set need not be symmetric or proper, so the picture must show only W_J within W_Theta rather than assert that a two-sector shape exhausts W_Theta.
findings.action: Appended a Remarks schematic of a small open arc J, unit normal theta, positive and negative signed frequencies, and the two sectors W_J subset W_Theta. Added captions tying direct vanishing to Fourier slice and global vanishing to compact-support analyticity and the existing proof.

correction: Added one explanatory TikZ figure and supporting Remarks only; original carrier remains an exact byte prefix.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Frequency plane R^2; unit circle S^1; a small open arc J subset Theta; W_J={sigma theta: theta in J, sigma nonzero}.
diagram_math_checks.check: The chosen 25-to-60 degree arc and its 205-to-240 degree antipode illustrate the small arc guaranteed by local F1. They represent a schematic subwedge, not the whole arbitrary W_Theta. Neither antipodal symmetry nor properness is imposed on Theta.

diagram_math_checks.objects: A normal theta at 42 degrees on S^1 and its dotted frequency line xi=sigma theta.
diagram_math_checks.check: The point has unit radius; the dotted line runs from angle 222 degrees to 42 degrees, so positive sigma is in J and negative sigma is in the antipodal sector. This matches F2 and the supplier Fourier-slice identity, not a tangent-line convention.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Excluded origin and sector boundary rays; finite display radius.
diagram_math_checks.check: W_J excludes sigma=0, indicated by the open center marker. Dashed boundary rays are excluded because J is open. The prose explicitly identifies the outer arcs as finite-radius truncation, not frequency cutoffs.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Direct measured-frequency vanishing and global Fourier vanishing.
diagram_math_checks.check: F2 and given zero Radon data imply vanishing on W_J; the original step 1.1 uses F3 coordinate-entire extension and F5 twice on a product rectangle to obtain vanishing on all real frequencies. Original step 2.1 then proves f=0. The explanatory text preserves that proof interface and makes no stability assertion.
